# Arvin Saghafi

> Arvin Saghafi (آروین ثقفی) is a backend-focused software developer and Computer Engineering student at the University of Tabriz, Iran. This site is his portfolio, with in-depth case studies of Rivo, a real-time encrypted chat application; OS, a mini operating system shell in C++ and Qt; WA Bank, a Java and JavaFX banking system; and Roof, a café's website and table booking system.
Arvin builds backend systems, REST APIs, real-time applications and database-driven software, with a particular interest in security and in interfaces that make complex systems feel simple.

## Projects

### Rivo

Rivo is a real-time chat application developed by Arvin Saghafi. Case study: https://www.aboutarvin.ir/rivo/

It was built to fix three things ordinary messengers get wrong:

- Every chat is treated the same. Rivo separates conversations automatically: a chat stays in "Active chats" as long as its last message has not been seen, by either side. Once the last message is seen and nobody replies, the conversation is over and it moves to "Contacts" on its own. A new message brings it back.
- Messages are permanent and instant. Rivo adds one-time messages, which can be opened only once, and time capsules, which are delivered locked and open at a moment the sender chooses.
- Archived chats never really leave. In most messengers an archived chat still sits on the main screen inside a folder. In Rivo, an archived chat disappears from the main screen entirely and is reachable only from Settings.

Security: Rivo uses envelope encryption. Each message is encrypted with a data key, and that data key is encrypted by a master key that never leaves HashiCorp Vault. The database stores only the ciphertext and the wrapped key, so a copy of the database on its own reveals nothing.

Technologies: Node.js, Express.js, Socket.IO, Prisma, PostgreSQL, HashiCorp Vault, JavaScript (ES modules), HTML, CSS.

### OS

OS is a mini operating system shell for the desktop, written by Arvin Saghafi in C++20 with Qt 6. It is not a kernel: it is the part people see and use. Case study: https://www.aboutarvin.ir/os/ Code: https://github.com/eros-codes/OS

He built it alone. It started as his first C++ project, a menu with a clock in it, and he rebuilt it from scratch around a real app model.

- Apps have a lifecycle: the OS creates an app when it opens, tells it when it moves to the background or returns, and destroys it when it is closed. Leaving an app does not close it: a game pauses, a timer keeps counting, music keeps playing.
- When a timer ends while another app is open, the OS rings and shows the notification over whatever is on screen. Alarm is a service that starts with the OS, so alarms ring even if the app was never opened. Recents lists every open app.
- Each app keeps its data in its own folder, and the OS shows how much each one uses.
- Vault stores passwords in one encrypted file. The master password is never stored; a key is derived from it with Argon2id (64 MB, 3 passes), and the data is encrypted with XChaCha20-Poly1305 with a fresh nonce on every save. A wrong password or any changed byte makes the file refuse to open. Its Argon2id implementation matches the RFC 9106 test vector.
- The music player's spectrum is real: each track is decoded in the background and every 40 ms of sound goes through an FFT into 20 bands.
- Apps can be installed from a plugin file. The OS's core is a shared library, oskit, that apps are built against. The OS reads a file's metadata without running its code before installing it. Apps must be granted permissions for notifications, the clipboard and files; installed apps ask the first time, and answers can be changed in App Info.
- The whole interface is drawn in dots: every icon is an 11 by 11 grid with one accent dot, and one renderer draws icons, clock rings, the spectrum and screen transitions.
- The OS was run under AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer through a scripted tour of every screen, with no memory errors, no undefined behaviour and no leaks from its own code.

Technologies: C++20, Qt 6 (Widgets, Multimedia), CMake, CTest, Monocypher.

### WA Bank

WA Bank is a desktop banking system built with Java, JavaFX and MySQL. Case study: https://www.aboutarvin.ir/bank/

It began as a university project that the team treated as a real product. It was built by three developers: two teammates built the JavaFX screens, and Arvin Saghafi wrote all of the Java behind them, including the application logic, the database layer, the validation and the interactive features.

WA Bank is three separate applications working on the same data: one for customers, one for employees and one for the bank manager. Its central idea is that online banking should feel like walking into a branch:

- Registration asks for personal details, a photo of the national ID card and a hand-drawn signature. Ticking "I accept" is not enough: the terms must actually be opened.
- A new account is created as Pending. Signing in is blocked until an employee reviews the ID photo and approves the account.
- Money is transferred between accounts by dragging your card onto the recipient's card. The closer it gets, the thicker the outline; letting go completes the transfer.
- On the card-to-card screen, the card fills in as you type, your own card number is suggested, and Enter completes the number and expiry date. The first six digits of a card number identify its bank.

Customer features: card, account and IBAN transfers (Paya, Satna and instant), deposits, loans, cheque books, bill payments and mobile top-ups. Employee features: verifying new customers, reviewing cheques and loan requests, transactions, deposits and financial reports. The manager's app includes everything an employee can do, plus managing employees and accounts.

Technologies: Java, JavaFX, FXML, CSS, MySQL, JDBC, Maven.

### Roof

Roof is a café's whole digital side: its website and menu, and a system for booking tables. Case study: https://www.aboutarvin.ir/roof/

The website was built entirely by Arvin Saghafi: a landing page, a menu split into café, restaurant and breakfast, and a feedback page, with an admin panel where staff manage products with photos, categories, guest reviews and admin accounts. Admins come in two roles, sign-in is rate-limited, and the dashboard counts each day's visits. Code: https://github.com/eros-codes/Cafe

The booking system was built by two developers: a teammate built the front end, including the interactive floor plan, and Arvin Saghafi built the back end: the API, the data model, the availability and booking engine, payments, SMS one-time codes and admin roles. Code: https://github.com/eros-codes/Restaurant-Reservation

- Guests choose their exact table on the café's real floor plan, not just a time slot. Tables that fit the group exactly are shown darker than tables with seats to spare.
- Each table has its own seat count and guest range; a six-seat table can also take a group of five.
- When no single table fits, connected tables are combined automatically, up to four tables.
- The layout is data: from the admin panel, tables can be moved, rotated and resized, chairs added or removed one by one, and seat counts and guest ranges set by hand. Owners and managers can edit; reception can only view.
- A booking is held for ten minutes while the guest pays. Checking availability and creating the hold happen in one serializable transaction, so a table can never be booked twice, and each booking keeps a fifteen-minute cleaning buffer.
- Guests sign in with SMS one-time codes, stored hashed with limited attempts. Prices come from server settings, never from the request. Payments go through Zarinpal.

Technologies: Node.js, Express.js, Prisma, PostgreSQL, Zod, JWT, bcrypt, Helmet.

### Shop

Shop is an e-commerce back end with a REST API, built by Arvin Saghafi with NestJS, TypeScript, TypeORM and MySQL. Its front end is in progress.

## Frequently asked questions

### Who is Arvin Saghafi?

Arvin Saghafi is a backend-focused software developer and Computer Engineering student at the University of Tabriz. He builds backend systems, REST APIs, real-time applications and database-driven software.

### What technologies does Arvin Saghafi use?

Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, C#, C++ and SQL; Node.js, Express.js, NestJS and Socket.IO on the backend; React, HTML and CSS on the frontend; PostgreSQL, MySQL, Prisma and TypeORM for data; JavaFX and Qt for desktop applications; and HashiCorp Vault, Argon2id and XChaCha20-Poly1305 for security.

### What projects has Arvin Saghafi built?

His selected work is Rivo, a real-time encrypted chat application; OS, a mini operating system shell in C++ and Qt; WA Bank, a Java and JavaFX banking system; Roof, a café's website and table booking system; and Shop, an e-commerce back end in NestJS.

### What is Rivo?

Rivo is a real-time chat application by Arvin Saghafi. It sorts chats automatically into Active chats and Contacts, supports one-time and time capsule messages, hides archived chats from the main screen, and encrypts every message with envelope encryption backed by HashiCorp Vault.

### How does Rivo decide which chats are active?

A chat stays in Active chats as long as its last message has not been seen. When the last message is seen and nobody replies, the conversation moves to Contacts. A new message moves it back.

### What is WA Bank?

WA Bank is a desktop banking system built with Java, JavaFX and MySQL, with separate applications for customers, employees and the bank manager. New accounts must be signed and approved by an employee before they can be used, and money is transferred by dragging one card onto another.

### What was Arvin Saghafi's role in WA Bank?

WA Bank was built by a team of three. Arvin Saghafi wrote all of the Java: the application logic, the database layer, the validation and the interactive features. His two teammates built the JavaFX screens.

### What is OS?

OS is a mini operating system shell for the desktop that Arvin Saghafi built alone in C++20 with Qt 6. Its apps keep working in the background, alarms and timers ring over whatever is open, a password vault encrypts everything with Argon2id and XChaCha20-Poly1305, apps can be installed from a file and must be granted permissions, and the interface is drawn in dots.

### What is Roof?

Roof is a café's website and table booking system. Arvin Saghafi built the website and its admin panel alone, and the booking system's back end with a teammate who built its front end. Guests pick their exact table on the café's real floor plan, and a serializable transaction makes double booking impossible.

### How can I contact Arvin Saghafi?

By email at saghafiarvin@gmail.com, or through GitHub at https://github.com/eros-codes.
